To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
two highly homologously HSP70s have opposing effects on protein aggregation and that these effects are caused by differences in the binding of specific co-chaperons to the HSP70 proteins.

two highly homologus HSP70s (HSPA1A and A1L) have opposing effects on the aggregation of the amyloidogenic protein SOD1-AV4, and that this difference is caused by differential interactions of these HSPs with the co-chaperone HSPH2.

two HSP70 paralogues have opposing effects on the fate of various protein substrates, including the aggregation-prone protein superoxide dismutas 1 (Sod1) A4V variant, which causes amyotrophic lateral sclerois (ALS).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of HSP70 paralogues in protein quality control.
the role of molecular chaperones in protein homeostasis and protein quality control.
the molecular mechanism of protein quality control.

HSPA1A is the major chaperone for SOD1-AV and HSPA1A/HSPH2 is the major chaser of SOD1-Av aggregates.

the HSP70 paralog HSPA1L has a more pronounced effect in enhancing the aggregation of the SOD1-AV4 protein than the HSP70 HSPA1A, and that this difference is determined by the differential binding affinity of HSP70s for the co-chaperone HSPH2.
the functional diversity between HSP 70 paralogs is determined by their variable interactions with specific chaperone co-factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the functional diversity between HSPs is caused by their variable interactions with specific cochaperones.
HSP70s are not redundant and that they can be functionally distinguished based on their differential interactions with co-chaperone proteins.
the HSPA1 paralogues HSPA1A, HSPA1B, and HSPA1C have a similar function, whereas the HSPA1L protein has a distinct function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Hsp70 chaperone system is more complex than we previously thought.
the cellular HSPs are not functionally redundant, but instead, each HSP has its own specific function, which is determined by the co-chaperones it interacts with.

the functional diversity between HSPs is not only defined by their substrate-binding domain, which has been the focus of many studies, but also by their differential interactions with specific co- chaperones.
